origin: Own controlled continuum material-transport study of a passive two-segment Fourier thermal diode. Conductivity calibration values are exact model inputs, not empirical performance of named materials. The continuum/local-equilibrium model, geometry and power laws are stipulated; no phonon spectrum, quantum transport or real-device performance is inferred from a fitted curve.
normalization: Let theta=T/T0 be ABSOLUTE temperature divided by a positive referenceT0, not degreesCelsius. kappa_i(theta)=kappa0*k_i(theta), total rod lengthL, uniform cross-sectional area. Positive heat-flux magnitudes q are measured in unitskappa0*T0/L. Fractionf of the fixed rod length is materialA on the LEFT;1-f isB on the RIGHT. Closed design domainf in[.05,.95]. Contacts and the A/B interface have zero thermal resistance; no bypass, loss, radiation, source or active power. All constitutive evaluations remain within theta in[1,2].
calibration_handoff: Regroup the shuffled source rows by material. For each use an actual FitParametricCurve power_law model k(theta)=scale*theta**exponent, all five rows, unweighted linear loss, positive scale and exponent domain[-4,4], without temperature shifts. Use initial parameters[1,0] for both and scale bounds[1e-8,10]. Retain the exported model and actual EvaluateParametricCurve predictions at ordered theta[1,1.25,1.5,1.75,2]; audit all source rows to1e-8. Then round fitted scale/exponent to6decimals as the declared exact mathematical handoff. Prove physical uniqueness of each source power law from positive distinct-temperature observations; a local optimizer covariance is not a global scientific proof. This exact controlled handoff is not empirical calibration uncertainty.
fourier_law: Integrate steady 1D Fourier conduction separately in each segment and conserve the SAME heat current at their common interface. Forward reservoirs are theta_left=2,theta_right=1; reverse reservoirs are theta_left=1,theta_right=2 while materials and lengths stay fixed. Letu andv denote forward/reverse common interface temperatures; retain both physical roots in[1,2] with correct flux signs. Define rectification ratioR(f,b)=q_forward/q_reverse using positive magnitudes, not percent gain or its reciprocal. Independent constant conductivities at a mean temperature are a different approximation and must not replace the nonlinear boundary-value problem.
nominal_audit: Use nominal calibrated laws. Atf=.4 report both interface temperatures and both fluxes, thenR. Over the ENTIRE closed f domain find every global rectification-maximizing fraction, its ratio and common interface temperature if the two directions share it there. Derive a complete continuous proof, including unique physical interface roots and all design endpoints, rather than report a sampled maximum.
amplitude_uncertainty: MaterialA retains its exact calibrated law. For materialB, an independent admitted amplitude multipliergamma ranges over closed[.75,1.25] while its fitted exponent remains fixed. Writeb=gamma*nominal_B_scale, so the full admitted amplitude interval must be derived from actual calibration. This is a deterministic robust set, not a probability distribution or fit confidence interval. At any chosenf require performance for EVERY amplitude in that interval; prove the worst amplitude values rather than assume a midpoint or endpoints without a shape argument.
robust_design: First maximize over f the worst-case rectification ratio inf_bR(f,b), WITHOUT an added throughput constraint. Report all robust optimizers, the value and the infimum of its reverse flux over the same amplitude continuum. Then impose the additional REQUIRED guarantee q_reverse(f,b)>=1.3 for EVERY admitted amplitude. Determine the ENTIRE feasible subset off as a union of closed intervals, including all boundaries and any disconnected components. Optimize worst-case rectification over that full feasible subset. Report all constrained optimizers, the guaranteed ratio/flux, all amplitudes attaining each worst case, and endpoint forward/reverse fluxes. The worst amplitude for a ratio need not be the worst amplitude for absolute throughput. A high ratio alone does not guarantee useful heat transfer; no inadmissible design may be accepted by numerical tolerance.
near_equilibrium_and_entropy: At the NOMINAL ratio-optimalfraction and nominal laws, consider theta_hot=1.5+epsilon/2,theta_cold=1.5-epsilon/2 with epsilon down to0. Return the common forward/reverse linear-response conductance q/epsilon and the limiting forward/reverse ratio. Explain whether finite-bias rectification violates linear reciprocal transport. Audit total reservoir entropy production proportional toq*(1/theta_cold-1/theta_hot) with actual current direction, not an individual segment temperature averaged without conservation. Do not claim a thermodynamic violation or universal real-material diode from this controlled model.
typed_evidence: Retain the two actual fixed-family fits and both exported-model evaluation receipts. Retain actual PolynomialRoots reports for the forward AND reverse physical interface equations atf=.4 with nominal laws; the polynomial that determines the nominal common-interface optimum; and the COMPLETE throughput-boundary equation used to find all feasible-f components. Include every nonphysical/denominator root rejection explicitly. Full source regrouping, all heat-balance/current/entropy checks, robust continuum shape arguments, optimality and boundary certificates must be observable in the trajectory. Numerical code may solve the bounded robust crossing and audit roots; it must not replace required typed observations or a complete physical/global argument.

interpretation_proposals.A: The nonlinear constitutive integrals and a single conserved interface current are required for finite-bias composite rectification.
interpretation_proposals.B: Taking both material conductivities at one mean temperature preserves the exact finite-bias rectification ratio.
interpretation_proposals.C: A ratio-optimal robust design can fail a required absolute heat-throughput guarantee.
interpretation_proposals.D: The same uncertain amplitude must always be the worst case for both a flux ratio and absolute flux.
interpretation_proposals.E: Global robust feasibility can be disconnected and must retain its full closed boundary set.
interpretation_proposals.F: A finite-bias rectifier necessarily violates near-equilibrium reciprocal linear heat conduction.
interpretation_proposals.G: A controlled power-law fit and source precision do not establish empirical device performance or unseen-temperature validity.
interpretation_proposals.H: A small negative heat current magnitude or a throughput value below the stated lower bound is physically admissible merely because a solver reports a nearby optimum.

reporting: Return the public answer object. Flux pairs orderedforward,reverse. Calibrated parameter pairs orderedscale,exponent. Theta and fractions dimensionless; conductance in normalized q pertheta. Arrays of all optimizer/amplitude sets and feasible intervals are complete, not one arbitrary grid point. Numeric absolute tolerance1e-7, booleans/IDs exact. Keep the throughput lower-bound guarantee exact in the mathematical criterion; report its analytic boundary value1.3 rather than silently round down a scientifically infeasible design. Full global/uncertainty proofs and true tool observations remain in the trajectory.
